news_posts.post_content: I recently came across a post from a self-taught data engineer who was looking to break into the big community of data professionals.  This person had learned SQL and completed a data engineering course, but was unsure of how to take the next step.  As someone who has been in the field for a while, I can relate to the feeling of not knowing where to start.  Here are a few key takeaways that I have learned along the way:  * Start by working on personal projects to gain practical experience,  * Seek out online communities and forums to connect with other data professionals,  * Don't be afraid to ask questions and seek help when you need it.  What are some other ways that self-taught data engineers can break into the field,  #dataengineering, #datascience, #careergoals

concept_posts.post_content: Have you ever wondered how to extend the functionality of your PostgreSQL database.  One way to do this is by using PostgreSQL extensions, such as PostGIS and pg_trgm.  These extensions can add new data types, functions, and operators to your database.  Some key points to consider when using PostgreSQL extensions include: * PostGIS allows you to store and query spatial data, such as points, lines, and polygons. * pg_trgm provides functions for determining the similarity between strings. * Extensions can be easily installed and removed using SQL commands. A common mistake to avoid is not checking the compatibility of an extension with your database version.  What is your experience with using PostgreSQL extensions,  #PostgreSQLExtensions  #PostGIS  #DatabaseManagement

concept_posts.post_content: Have you ever wondered how to streamline your data engineering workflow,  making it more efficient and reliable.  A key concept to explore is DataOps and CI/CD for Data,  which involves applying DevOps principles to data engineering.  For instance, a company can use DataOps to automate their data pipeline,  ensuring that data is processed and delivered quickly and accurately.  Some key points to consider are:  * Automating data testing and validation,  * Implementing continuous integration and deployment,  * Monitoring data quality and performance.  A common mistake to avoid is not prioritizing data quality and testing.  What strategies do you use to ensure data quality and reliability in your organization,  #DataEngineering,  #DataOps,  #CICD
